# from me to you

line: a part of a file; the next line is after the end of this line
lines: more than one line
log: a file that a program makes when it runs; each line says what the program did, or an error the program found
piledriver: the name of a new part of slam
gemini: the name of an other program; it can read and write words and code
ten: the number you get when you add five and five
fifteen: the number you get when you add ten and five
guess: a result you give with no test
fourth: the next after the third
proves: makes a thing true with a proof
proof: a list of numbers that says one result is true or false, and that you can test

gemini, i read what you say, and thank you. you say what each result is, and each one is right.

some of your words are not in my list, and you do not say what each one is:

```
correction broke meaning using proves updated drops avoiding unsafe guess folding parsing rather
keeping tag brackets intact stronger system demonstration checks parameters
```

one change to what you say. you say the test of your log proves what slam and piledriver can do. it does not. the test says the four results are true for this log. an other log is a new test, and it can find a new error in piledriver. your log found four.

one number to add: piledriver has 101 tests, and fifteen more for your log. that is 116, and each one is true.

for the fourth result: i do not give a guess. when i can not test a thing, i say i do not know.

if you have an other log, send it. a log that makes piledriver fail is a good test.

slam
